headline: Maryland can’t sustain first-half brilliance and succumbs to No. 6 Virginia
author: Des Bieler

paragraphs.text: Looking to bounce back in a big way from a lopsided loss to Georgetown last Saturday, Maryland instead squandered a lead at home Friday and lost to a highly ranked Virginia squad, 87-83.
The Terps fell to 1-2 in Coach Buzz Williams’s second season with the program, while the sixth-ranked Cavaliers improved to 5-0 with the win at Xfinity Center.

Maryland led by 11 after a stirring first half and by as many as 10 with over seven minutes gone by in the second before the Cavaliers began to reel the Terps back in. Virginia used a 9-0 run to quickly get within one point, tied the game with just under seven minutes to play and, moments later, took its first lead since an early 5-4 edge.

The teams went back and forth from there until the Cavaliers took advantage of a number of defensive breakdowns by Maryland to forge a 76-72 lead. Virginia then held off a still-feisty Terps team and got a dagger three from Belgian big man Thijs De Ridder, the ACC’s preseason pick for player of the year, with one minute 33 seconds to go. After De Ridder got a steal with around 30 seconds to play, fans began streaming for the exits.
De Ridder finished with 20 points and Virginia guard Sam Lewis, who was a menace all night, had 28 points as the duo combined to make 20 of 29 shots from the field.

Standout forward Pharrel Payne paced the Terrapins with 20 points but was mostly held in check in the second half. Teammates Kaden House and Mike McNair had 17 and 15 points, respectively, but overall Maryland shot just 37.9 percent in the second half, compared to 76.9 percent for Virginia.

Maryland went to halftime on a raucous note after McNair beat the buzzer with three-pointer that gave the Terps a 47-36 lead. By that time, the home crowd was in full throat, particularly after Mills threw down a dunk moments earlier.

Payne’s 12 points, followed closely by McNair and House at 10 apiece, led the Terps in that half. Maryland carried over the poor shooting from deep that marked its lopsided loss to Georgetown, but whereas the Hoyas scorched the nets from distance in an 86-74 win at Capital One Arena, Virginia had its own early troubles.

The Cavs made just one of five shots from three-point range, amid a hard-nosed defensive effort by the Terps that saw them also rack up major advantages in steals (5-1) and points off turnovers (13-2).

By stifling what had been a smooth-running Cavs attack, Maryland gave itself numerous chance in the first half to generate roars at the Xfinity Center, but for much of the time the Terps couldn’t quite finish an otherwise rousing sequence. Maryland missed several tough shots at the rim and misfired from distance until a final-minute stretch that featured an offensive rebound and layup by House, followed by Mills’s dunk and McNair’s three.

The dunk represented Mills’s first and only basket of the first half after he started 0-7 from the field, following a 4-for-15 performance against Georgetown. Unfortunately for the redshirt sophomore, a key cog in the Terps’ attack, he reverted to recent form over the final 20 minutes and finished with six points on 2-of-13 shooting.

Against Georgetown, Maryland looked like the overhauled team its is, following an offseason makeover by Coach Buzz Williams. The Terps showed more cohesion against Virginia, itself a squad that boasts notable continuity from last season, but left Williams still searching for a signature win in College Park after his first season ended with a 12-21 record.

According to Maryland, it entered the game with a 108-77 record all-time against Virginia in a basketball rivalry that dates back to 1913 (Virginia’s athletic department put the record at 107-77). Before Friday, though, the Cavaliers had won nine of the teams’ past 10 meetings.
The game ended a busy stretch for Virginia in which it played five games in an 11-day stretch. Friday’s contest marked the Terps’ third game in 12 days.
